ch02.before: Wang Leping and Wang Yaqiao went back years in Shanghai
ch02.caption: Wang Leping (third row, second from left), Wang Yaqiao's good friend and a core figure of the Reorganizationists' military campaign against Chiang, in the group photograph of delegates to the Third Plenum of the Kuomintang's Second Central Executive Committee, March 10, 1927. Front row, from left: Ding Weifen, Gu Mengyu, Xu Qian, Tan Yankai, Sun Ke, Soong Ching-ling, T.V. Soong, Eugene Chen, Jing Hengyi, Wu Yuzhang. Middle row: second from left, Dong Biwu; third from right, Mao Zedong. Caption as given in the original edition.

ch06.before: the Nakamura affair in Manchuria is the best example there is
ch06.caption: In June 1931 Captain Nakamura Shintaro of the Japanese General Staff and three companions entered the Greater Khingan region of China illegally to carry out espionage, and were seized and put to death by the Chinese garrison. Japan used the affair to move large reinforcements into the northeast, and shortly afterward launched the September 18th Incident. Caption as given in the original edition.
ch06.alt: Two men standing on either side of a horse

ch06.before: Liu Haichuan nodded and nodded again.

ch06.before: Shigemitsu turned an ingratiating, smiling face
ch06.caption: Shigemitsu Mamoru (right), Japanese consul-general at Shanghai and minister to China, never imagined that he would become the sacrificial victim in the Japanese military's manufacture of a pretext for invading China. This photograph shows him in 1930 with Wang Zhengting, foreign minister of the Nanjing National Government. Caption as given in the original edition.
ch06.alt: Two men in suits shaking hands
